newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's leading economist Simonsen dies at 61.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's leading economist Simonsen dies at 61.

text.p: Former Planning and Finance Minister Mario Henrique Simonsen, one of Brazil's leading economists, died of lung cancer in Rio de Janeiro, a hospital spokeswoman said on Monday. He was 61.
Simonsen, who had been suffering from lung cancer for the past two years, died on Sunday night. His funeral was scheduled to be held on Monday, the spokeswoman said.
He became known as one of the architects of Brazil's "economic miracle" in the 1970s when he served as planning and finance minister under the then-military dictatorship.
He coined the term "Belgindia" to describe Brazil as incorporating two types of countries, Belgium and India, in the same territory -- one rich and developed, and the other poor and underdeveloped.

The opera-loving economist continued his career as a director of U.S. Citibank for 15 years, leaving his post in July 1995 for health reasons. In later years, he became one of Brazil's most respected independent economists, working for the economic think tank Fundacao Getulio Vargas.
